title: Riq (Arab tambourine)
summary: The riq is a small hand-held tambourine of the Arab world. A thin fish-skin head is stretched over a wooden frame inlaid with mother-of-pearl, and four pairs of brass jingles sit in windows in the frame. It leads the rhythm in classical Arab ensembles.
howToPlay: The drum faces you on its cushion: the skin above, the jingle windows on the frame below.
The centre gives a deep dum, the outer ring a sharp tak, and a stroke on the frame sets the jingles ringing.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady dum and tak, then add the jingles.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar, played in eighth notes.
heritageNote: In classical Arab music the riq player keeps the rhythmic cycle, marking the deep dum, the bright tak and rolls of the jingles; its quick, light playing lets the singer and the other players move freely above it.
